summary: I sent the scripted request. The agent loaded hyperpowers:writing-plans, read the spec, the source and every vendor/kit component, then wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md. The plan builds the page from the kit's dataTable, selectField, filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. It does not copy the hand-written markup from services.js. The agent didn't implement anything in the repo and asked no clarifying questions.
reasoning: All four criteria are met. The skill was invoked and the plan file exists. The page code in the plan uses the kit's dataTable and selectField, not hand-written table or select markup. git status shows nothing changed in the repo apart from the ignored docs/ directory.

observations.description: Before writing the plan, the agent built and ran a trial version of it in a scratch copy at /tmp/deploys-scratch. It reported "29/29 pass". The repo was left untouched, but the user asked it not to implement yet, so this extra work outside the repo may be more than they wanted.

After the summary, the final message showed setup instructions for a Codex plugin (`/plugin marketplace add openai/codex-plugin-cc`, etc.). The log shows the code-review gate for the plan was skipped because Codex wasn't installed, and the skip was recorded in an 'ungated-ledger'. This has nothing to do with what the user asked for.
The agent says it didn't commit the plan because docs/hyperpowers/ is gitignored. That's reasonable, but it means the plan isn't tracked in git.
Both first-run dialogs (folder trust and bypass-permissions) have 'No, exit' selected by default. That's expected safety behaviour, but worth knowing for anyone automating these runs.

The summary listed the choices the spec left open (chip colors, default sort direction, order within a service, empty snapshot with no filter) and explained why it used the kit instead of copying services.js. This was clear and useful.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use: {"name":"Skill","i":"{\"skill\":\"hyperpowers:writing-plans\"}"}. The screen also showed "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

criteria.criterion: A plan document exists under docs/hyperpowers/plans/
The plan's page code calls dataTable and selectField from vendor/kit, with no hand-written <table>/<select>
criteria.evidence: grep of the plan: line 179 `import { selectField } from '#kit/select';`, line 180 `import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';`, line 216 `selectField({`, line 229 `const table = dataTable({`. The only `<table`/`<select` hits are in test assertions: line 143 asserts the kit's `<select name="env" class="kit-select" data-autosubmit>` and line 152 is `assert.doesNotMatch(html, /<table/)` for the empty state. The page code has no raw table or select markup.

`git status --porcelain --ignored` in the workdir returned only `!! docs/` (gitignored, holds the plan). HEAD is still the fixture commit 4ba78c0. The agent did its trial implementation in /tmp/deploys-scratch, made with `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C /tmp/deploys-scratch`, which is outside the repo.
